newsitem.title: FINLAND: EMU MAY CONCENTRATE GROWTH TO CORE EUROPE - MTK.
newsitem.headline: EMU MAY CONCENTRATE GROWTH TO CORE EUROPE - MTK.

text.p: The head of Finland's farming lobby warned on Tuesday that economic activity and growth might become concentrated in core European areas as a result of monetary union.

"The biggest risk with the single currency area is that economic activity, well-being and growth will be concentrated in the core European areas, on the Frankfurt-Paris axis," Central Union of Agricultural Producers and Forest Owners (MTK) chairman Esa Harmala told Reuters in an interview.
"And so other areas will be pushed into the periphery in economic development," he added.

Another clear drawback will be that membership of the third stage of European economic and monetary union (EMU) marks the end to national currencies, and exposes businesses to fierce competion, Harmala said.
"National currencies have protected businesses and sectors that wouldn't survive in the single currency area," he said.
Looking at the bright side, Harmala said agriculture, like other businesses, could also benefit from a single currency.
"In monetary union, the market area will increase ten-fold and foreign currency exchange rate costs will be eliminated," he said.

But countries in EMU would become "extremely sensitive" to higher costs elsewhere and Finland, which used to correct imbalances by devaluing its currency, may not endure, in a fixed exchange rate regime, Harmala said.
For the forest industry, it would be "sheer madness" if Finland joined the third stage of EMU without Sweden, he said.
The U.S. dollar is the main invoicing currency for pulp and paper, and the Swedish crown is the central invoicing currency for mechanical forest industry products, he noted.
